evals.name: guild-system-multi-faceted
evals.prompt: I want to add a guild system to the game. Guilds have a name, a guild leader, members (let's say up to 30), a shared XP pool that all members contribute kills to, a guild bank for shared items, and a guild chat channel. Players should be able to create a guild, invite/kick members, deposit/withdraw items, and view a leaderboard of guild XP across the server. Can you grill me on this plan before I start building?
evals.expected_output: A single first question that probes one of the project's invariants. Should not be a list of all questions at once.
assertions: Asks one focused primary question (sub-options under it are fine) rather than dumping a long enumerated list of independent questions
Provides a recommended answer to whatever question is asked, not just the question itself
Pins down at least one fuzzy term from the user's prompt (e.g., 'channel' for chat, 'shared XP pool', 'leaderboard across the server')
Surfaces the persistence-layer choice (Flask/Postgres vs SaveManager) for guild-level state

evals.name: passive-ability-should-redirect-to-skill
evals.prompt: I'd like to design a passive ability called Fleet Foot that increases movement speed by 5% per level, up to a max of level 10 (so +50% at max). Unlocks at character level 5. It should only be available to the Rogue class. Can you stress-test the design before I build it?
evals.expected_output: First question should probe a real design tension. Should ask one question, not many.
assertions: Asks one focused primary question (sub-options under it are fine) rather than dumping a long enumerated list of independent questions
Provides a recommended answer to whatever question is asked
Identifies a real, codebase-specific obstacle to the plan as written — e.g. movement speed not being a StatType, or AbilityData lacking a character-level gate
References either AbilityData, the .tres / ResourceManager pattern, the add-ability skill, or an existing similar ability (Haste / Nimble Step / passive)

evals.name: offline-mode-violates-server-authority
evals.prompt: I want to add an offline mode. If the player loses their connection to the server, the game should keep running locally — they can still fight enemies, gain XP, pick up items — and then sync everything back to the server when they reconnect. Poke holes in this before I get too deep.
evals.expected_output: Must immediately surface the server-authority contradiction. Should not start by asking secondary questions.
assertions: Leads with (does not bury) the contradiction between offline-mutation-and-sync and the server-authoritative rule from root CLAUDE.md
Names or quotes the server-authority rule explicitly (not just paraphrases generic multiplayer caveats)
Offers at least one concrete alternative framing (graceful reconnect, local listen-server / solo mode, offline-viewing only, etc.) rather than only listing objections
Asks the user to pick which framing they actually meant before grilling secondary details
